# Creating trajectories

This section outlines the process for creating trajectories, including handling edge cases.

The standard approach involves using the default configuration, data import, and pre-processing steps, as described in [getting started](a00_introduction.html#study-configuration).

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
trajectories <- createTrajectories(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)
```

Keep the configured `studyEnv` in every call and first run
`getDataForStudy()` successfully. For a fresh study, individual generation
settings can be overridden. For example, generate discrete trajectories in
30-day cycles:

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
trajectories <- createTrajectories(
  cdm = cdm,
  studyEnv = studyEnv,
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  lengthOfStay = 30
)
```

For a saved study configured with `runSavedStudy = TRUE`, use its restored
settings without analytical overrides. Import fresh data before generation:

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
getDataForStudy(cdm = newCdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(cdm = newCdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)
```

## Adding personal data to self-inserted data

To join patient age and gender from a CDM while creating trajectories, supply the CDM object and set `useCDM = TRUE`.
With `useCDM = FALSE`, both trajectory formats include `age` and `gender_concept_id` as `NA` in the returned data and exported CSV. No birth date is assumed. This replaces the earlier placeholder gender code and `birth_datetime = "1900-01-01"` column.

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
trajectories <- createTrajectories(
  cdm = cdm,
  studyEnv = studyEnv,
  useCDM = TRUE
)
```

The function returns a dataframe with the trajectories and saves the trajectories to the study path.
